text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm opening a docs PR for the new 'Orion-XL-LongCtx' model card. Found a couple of compatibility quirks we should call out and want quick eyes on the SDK snippet before I merge.

maria: Main items: 1) context_len vs usable_context due to tokenization; 2) quant profile compatibility for CPU fallback; 3) example showing streaming + function-calls.

tom: can you paste the snippet you're planning to include?

maria: Sure — current draft for SDK v3 usage (streaming + function call):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$RW_KEY")

with client.chat.stream(model="orion-xl-longctx") as s:
    s.call_function("split_paragraphs")
    for chunk in s:
        print(chunk.text, end="")
```

maria: This is terse; wondering if we should show the full function schema example too.

kai: two quick notes: 1) 'usable_context' is typically ~-20 tokens from reported context_len for orion; we should show the explicit math so users don't hit truncation surprises. 2) quant profile: the 4-bit CPU fallback is only compatible with 'profile-lite' not 'profile-compat'. Add a compatibility table?

jen: +1 to table. Also, our benchmark numbers in the model card are from seq=2048; but default bench harness used 1024 in the catalog. We should align and note that latency scales non-linearly for longctx.

sam: I can update the benchmark note and add a small chart (1024 vs 2048 vs 4096) — will attach graph to the PR.

maria: thanks — can you also call out that embeddings are blocked for this family (internal policy), i.e., model isn't supported for embedding endpoints? Documenting prevents accidental usage.

kai: Good catch. Add a line: "Not available for embeddings — use 'Orion-Embed' family instead."

maria: For SDK snippet: should I include both v2 and v3 examples, or link to migration guide?

tom: put v3 primary, v2 as a one-liner and link to migration guide. Most new users should see v3 first.

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5423 — draft with TODOs for the table and benchmarks.

docs-bot: PR 5423 created by maria — status: draft. CI checks queued. :github:

ci-bot: CI started — spellcheck, lint, linkcheck.

jen: I'll do a quick review after CI passes. Also suggest a small snippet showing 'usable_context' calculation: e.g.,
```
# reported max sequence: 8192
# reserved for system/meta tokens: ~32
usable_context = reported_max - reserved - prompt_padding
```

maria: Adding that. Also adding a note about model fallback routing: if Dedicated capacity isn't compatible, Hosted will automatically route to 'orion-xl-longctx-compat' (slower but supported). We should list the exact variant name.

sam: Added bench updates and attached png. I also updated the example prompts to include explicit end-of-turn tokens so streaming examples are deterministic.

tom: CI passed for markdown lint and linkcheck but found one broken link to sdk v3 reference — PR failing linkcheck.

maria: fixed link (was pointing to /sdk/reference/v3 -> should be /sdk/v3/reference). Pushed.

docs-bot: PR 5423 updated by maria — status: open.

jen: Quick LGTM from me on content. One nit: change '4-bit CPU fallback' wording to '4-bit quantized CPU fallback (profile-lite only)'.

maria: updated wording, added compatibility table, included v2 one-liner and migration link, and included the graph. Ready for merge if no more blockers.

kai: looked through the table — please add an explicit row for 'streaming + function-calls' interoperability (works, but increased memory with large schemas).

maria: done. Merging after an hour to give people time to object. If no objections I'll squash-merge. :hourglass: 

tom: no objections. Thanks for moving quickly. :rocket:

maria: merged and published. Release note: updated model catalog entry for orion-xl-longctx clarifying usable_context, CPU quant profile compatibility, embedding policy, streaming/function-call caveat, and benchmark appendix (PR 5423).

docs-bot: PR 5423 merged by maria — status: merged. Release deployed to staging docs site.

ci-bot: deploy succeeded to staging — smoke tests passed.

sam: will open a follow-up issue to track telemetry after release to see if users hit truncation errors. Issue #3124.

maria: great, thanks everyone!
